_comment: Kill-mutations, one per guard whose SHAPE is prone to going vacuous. Run by
tools/mutation-check.mjs and by the `mutation` CI job: each mutant is applied to the working
tree, the suite is run, and the named guard MUST fail. A mutant that survives means that guard
WHAT BELONGS HERE. Not every assertion: value-equality tests have essentially never gone vacuous
in this repo. What has, six times out of ~35 new guards in one session, is the EXISTENCE shape --
a claim checked over a search space far larger than its subject (a substring of the whole source,
an accessible name matched with `includes`, `the menu offered something`, a source-ORDER pin).
Add a mutant when a guard asserts that something EXISTS, IS PRESENT, or HAPPENED. Skip it when
kills = a substring of the failing test's name. file/find/replace = one exact, UNIQUE edit; the
runner refuses to proceed if `find` does not match exactly once, because a find string that has
drifted would apply nothing and the mutant would 'survive' for a reason unrelated to the guard.
suite:'browser' entries are recorded but not run by default -- a driven run costs ~80s against
~5s for the unit suite. The runner prints what it skipped rather than skipping silently.
